The complaint, refiled on Thursday in California federal court, argues that combining the streaming services could reduce competition, limit consumer choice, and lead to higher subscription costs. Plaintiffs are also challenging Skydance's
plans to achieve at least $6 billion in annualized cost savings over three years, arguing that operational consolidation and workforce reductions could hurt programming diversity.
The consumers are seeking to reverse the Warner Bros. (WBD) acquisition, as well as the earlier Paramount-Skydance
merger, or require the divestiture of assets including HBO Max, CNN, and Warner Bros. (WBD) studio operations. They are also asking the court to keep the two streaming platforms separate.
